newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway 1996 budget surplus seen at 37.9 bln crowns.
newsitem.headline: Norway 1996 budget surplus seen at 37.9 bln crowns.

text.p: The Norwegian government upgraded its forecast for this year's budget surplus on Friday to 37.9 billion crowns from 24.9 billion in a forecast made in May to account for soaring oil prices.
In its 1997 draft budget, the government forecast the surplus at 40.9 billion crowns.
The new forecast takes into account an oil price of 125 crowns per barrel this year, compared with 115 crowns in the previous forecast.
For 1997, it saw an oil price of 115 crowns per barrel compared with 105 crowns earlier.

Excluding petroleum revenues, the government said next year's budget would have a deficit of 24.2 billion crowns. For 1996, the budget would show a deficit of 25.9 billion crowns, discounting petroleum activities, it said.
